title: `LIKE`, `contains`, `startswith`, `instr`, `RLIKE`, `replace` are case-sensitive
verdict: `case_sensitivity: CASE_SENSITIVE`; `ILIKE` and `(?i)` for the other, `(?i)` ASCII only
description: `'ABC' LIKE 'a%'`, `contains('ABC', 'b')`, `startswith('ABC', 'a')`, `endswith('ABC', 'c')`, `'ABC' RLIKE 'b'` are false and `instr('ABC', 'b')` is 0: every match function compares code points exactly, and so does `=` under the default `UTF8_BINARY` collation. `ILIKE` folds case. In a regex, `(?i)` folds ASCII only (`'É' RLIKE '(?i)é'` is false) unless `(?iu)` is given.
`LIKE` escapes with `\` by default or `ESCAPE`; `_` matches one code point (`'é' LIKE '_'`). `startswith(s, '')` is true.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `regexp_count('the fox', 'FOX')` is 0: regex matching is case-sensitive
`'A' ilike 'a'` is true: ILIKE folds case
`'a_%b' ilike 'a\\__b'` is true: `\` escapes `_` by default
`'A€a' ilike '_€_'` is true: `_` matches one code point, `€` being three UTF-8 bytes

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
